messages.content: In the 2017 paper by Abdiaj and Alcázar on transferring dual photoredox/nickel catalysis from batch to flow, what was the root cause of reactor blockage in the initial flow experiments, which base-solvent combination solved it, and what temperature and residence time gave the best isolated yield?

**Background**

Flow chemistry involves performing chemical reactions in a continuously pumped microchannel or tubing system rather than in traditional static batch reactors, enabling precise thermal control, enhanced mixing, and safer handling of reactive intermediates. Dual catalysis simultaneously employs two distinct catalytic cycles—commonly a visible-light-driven photoredox system paired with a transition-metal cross-coupling catalyst—to achieve complex bond formations that neither catalyst could accomplish alone. Translating these sensitive, multicomponent reaction manifolds from batch to flow often encounters practical engineering obstacles like solid precipitate accumulation, but when successfully scaled, continuous processing significantly improves reaction throughput, reproducibility, and overall sustainability in modern organic synthesis.

---

Based on the provided summaries, the initial flow experiments suffered from reactor blockage due to the precipitation of insoluble material, which was attributed to the formation of the corresponding HBr salt of the base when tested in solvents such as THF, acetone, toluene, and ethyl acetate [Abdiaj et al., 2017]. This operational failure was resolved by implementing 1,5-diazabiciclo[5.4.0]undec-5-ene (DBU) paired with dimethylformamide (DMA) as the base-solvent combination, a pairing that maintained complete solubility and delivered the highest conversion during parallel batch screenings [Abdiaj et al., 2017]. When transferring these optimized conditions to a continuous flow setup, adjusting reaction parameters improved the product purity; the highest isolated yield was ultimately obtained operating at 60 °C with a residence time of 20 minutes [Abdiaj et al., 2017]. While these excerpts comprehensively address the specified operational parameters, they do not provide further details on the exact molecular identity of the precipitate, broader substrate scope limitations, or extended kinetic profiling of the flow residence time optimization.
